problem: The point $P$ has polar coordinates $(4,{225}^{∘}).$ Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P.$

feedback.problem:
If the point $P$ has polar coordinates $(2,\frac{\pi }{2}),$ then its Cartesian coordinates are$\,(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
feedback.worked_solution:
To convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we calculate the $x$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ x & =2\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\ x & =2\cdot 0 \\ x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the $y$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ y & =2\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\ y & =2\cdot 1 \\ y & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(0,2).$
